brands.name: Morrow Goods
brands.description: Fictional demo brand — a home and lifestyle goods company. These rules are illustrative demo rules, not verified facts about a real company.

rules.name: Absolute Environmental Claim
rules.description: Absolute environmental claims like '100% sustainable' or 'zero impact' are difficult to substantiate and may mislead consumers. Regulatory guidance (e.g., FTC Green Guides, UK CMA) recommends specific, qualified claims instead.
rules.suggestion: Replace with specific, measurable claims (e.g., 'made with 80% recycled materials' or 'reduces packaging waste by 40%').

rules.name: Restricted Phrases
rules.description: Words like 'guaranteed', 'miracle', and 'risk-free' imply absolute certainty that rarely exists in practice. These trigger mandatory human review per Morrow Goods policy.
rules.suggestion: Use qualified language (e.g., 'designed to reduce risk', 'clinically tested', 'backed by our warranty').

rules.name: Vague Superlatives
rules.description: Vague superlatives cannot be verified and may appear as puffery. Morrow Goods tone prefers specific, grounded language.
rules.suggestion: Replace with concrete differentiators (e.g., 'rated 4.8/5 by 2,000+ customers', 'uses 30% less energy than standard models').
